body:
Coordinator lesson (Termal::Fable2, 2026-11-24, w-56f386fdd7d3: 53 candidates, 39 review rounds, 9+ evaluations).

When consecutive review rounds keep finding NEW interleavings in the same sub-area (here, following any-wait runs that were not yet indexed as finished; 2 to 4 new ones per round over 11 rounds), the fixes are not converging: each mechanism added widens the surface for the next round.

Rule: after about 3 rounds of that pattern, stop fixing case by case.
- Cut the sub-area out with an explicit limit in the criterion, tracked as its own item (here w-a6eefa5cc561, with the rounds' findings as its test corpus).
- Remove the machinery built for it.
- Rule later findings in that area against the new limit and file them.

That is a deliberate scope decision with a stated limit, not rewording to pass. Ask the coder early whether the surface is converging. Here Opus3 raised it himself at round 39.
